question: How many resource cards does a city normally produce when an adjacent hex produces resources?
expected_answer: Two cards of that hex's resource.

question: Can I build another settlement on my first turn after setup?
expected_answer: Yes, during the Action phase, if you can pay its cost, connect it to your road, obey the Distance Rule, and have a settlement available. Setup does not guarantee that you can meet those conditions.

question: Is every development card forbidden from being used on the turn you buy it?
expected_answer: No. Victory Point cards bought that turn may be revealed if they give you enough points to win.

question: In CATAN, how many resource cards can I hold without discarding when a 7 is rolled? Do development cards count?
expected_answer: Seven resource cards. A player with more than seven discards half, rounded down. Development cards do not count.
notes: Relabeled from disambiguation: answer combines two sections.

question: What penalty does the CATAN rulebook impose for flipping over the board?
expected_answer: Not specified in the supplied rulebook.

question: According to the pictured building-cost diagram, what does a development card cost?
expected_answer: One wool, one wheat, and one ore.
notes: Expected baseline failure: costs are icons only; text extraction yields just 'BUILDING COST:'.

question: How much money do you collect when you pass or land on GO?
expected_answer: 200 in game money from the Bank.
notes: Currency symbol extracts as the letter 'a' (e.g. 'a200').

question: If you own a complete colour set while in Jail, may you buy Houses? What building restrictions still apply?
expected_answer: Yes. You must pay the Title Deed cost and build evenly; you cannot build if a street in that set is mortgaged.
source_section: Building Houses; Building Hotels; Go To Jail
notes: Monopoly has only 2 large pages; score at section level.

question: Do you collect money for landing on Free Parking?
expected_answer: No. Nothing happens; the rulebook gives no Free Parking bonus.

question: In Monopoly, does rolling doubles always grant another turn?
expected_answer: No. Doubles normally grant another turn, but three doubles in a row send you immediately to Jail.
notes: Relabeled from disambiguation: single-section exception rule.

question: What does this rulebook require if a die falls off the board?
expected_answer: Not specified in the supplied rulebook.

question: On the illustrated Pentonville Road Title Deed, what is the rent with three Houses?
expected_answer: 300 in game money.
notes: Expected baseline failure: house icons are stripped; rent rows lose their house counts.

question: In four-player Standard Rummy, how many cards is each player dealt?
expected_answer: Seven.

question: In five-player Standard Rummy, the player left of the dealer already holds a valid set. How many cards were they dealt, and may they meld before drawing?
expected_answer: Six cards; no, they must draw before melding.
source_section: Dealing the cards; The Deal; Game Play

question: Can a player go out in Standard Rummy by melding every remaining card without discarding?
expected_answer: No. The standard rule requires a final discard. Going out without one is an optional variation.
source_section: End of Hand; Optional Rules (Lazy go out)

question: In Standard Rummy, how many points is an Ace left in an opponent's hand worth under the default rule?
expected_answer: One point; a high-Ace rule is optional.
notes: Within-game variant disambiguation (default vs optional rule).

question: How many seconds may a Standard Rummy player take before receiving a time penalty?
expected_answer: Not specified in the supplied rulebook.

question: At what hand total may the dealer stop taking cards?
expected_answer: At 17 or higher; the dealer must hit until reaching at least 17.

question: What happens to your original bet on a push?
expected_answer: It is returned.

question: Your initial two cards are an Ace and a Queen. What is their total, and what payout does the book list for that hand?
expected_answer: 21; it is blackjack and is paid at 3:2.

question: Does insurance pay if you win your main hand but the dealer does not have blackjack?
expected_answer: No. Insurance pays 2:1 only if the dealer's hidden card has a value of 10, giving the dealer blackjack. The side bet is separate from the main hand.

question: In Blackjack, is an Ace always worth one point, as it is by default in Standard Rummy?
expected_answer: No. A Blackjack Ace may count as 1 or 11.

question: Does this Blackjack rulebook allow doubling down after splitting a pair?
expected_answer: Not specified. It describes splitting and doubling down separately but gives no rule for combining them.
notes: Most LLMs 'know' a casino answer; strong hallucination test.

question: For a Poker game with seven or more players, what minimum total supply of chips does the book recommend?
expected_answer: At least 200 chips for the game.

question: In the book's pot-limit example, six chips are in the pot and someone bets four. After calling, how many additional chips may the next player raise by?
expected_answer: 14 additional chips; the player puts in 18 total, including the four-chip call.
notes: The book works this exact example.

question: A player checks, then faces a bet later in the round and folds. Must they call that bet, and do they recover chips already committed to the pot?
expected_answer: They need not call if they fold, but they lose chips already committed to that pot.

question: Can suit ranking break a tie between otherwise equal Poker hands?
expected_answer: No. Suits have no relative rank; tied players split the pot.

question: In Draw Poker, are a player's cards face up as some are in Stud Poker?
expected_answer: No. Draw Poker deals all cards face down; Stud Poker deals some face up.

question: What exact penalty does this Poker rulebook prescribe for exposing a hand before the final betting round?
expected_answer: Not specified in the supplied rulebook.

question: How many private hole cards is each player dealt?
expected_answer: Two.

question: If nobody bets during the final betting round, who shows their cards first at showdown?
expected_answer: The remaining player immediately clockwise from the button.

question: After betting on the flop ends, which community card is dealt next, and who acts first in the next betting round?
expected_answer: The turn, which is the fourth community card; betting starts with the first active player immediately clockwise from the button.

question: Must a player use both hole cards to make their final five-card hand?
expected_answer: No. They may use zero, one, or two hole cards.

question: In Texas Hold'em, who posts the big blind relative to the dealer button?
expected_answer: The player immediately clockwise from the small blind, who is immediately clockwise from the button.

question: What fixed minimum buy-in does this Texas Hold'em rulebook require?
expected_answer: Not specified in the supplied rulebook.

question: Can jokers be used in the deck?
expected_answer: General poker: a standard 52-card pack is used, sometimes with one or two jokers added, often as wild cards. Texas Hold'em: the book specifies a standard 52-card pack; jokers appear only in its note that five of a kind requires a wild card.
source_section: The Pack; Wild Cards; The Pack

question: What is the first forced bet in a hand?
expected_answer: General poker: an ante, if the game's rules require one. Texas Hold'em: the small blind, posted by the player immediately clockwise from the button; an ante may also be required depending on the structure.

question: What happens if there's a tie?
expected_answer: Ambiguous: depends on the game. Blackjack: a push returns your bet. Poker: identical hands split the pot. Texas Hold'em: the pot is divided equally between the best hands.
notes: No game named. Decide whether the system should ask which game or answer per game.

question: What is an Ace worth?
expected_answer: Ambiguous: depends on the game. Blackjack: 1 or 11. Standard Rummy: 1 by default, or 15 under the high-Ace variation. Poker: ranks high, so an ace-high hand beats a king-high hand.
source_section: Card Values/scoring; Setup; Optional Rules; No Pair

question: Who goes first?
expected_answer: Ambiguous: depends on the game. CATAN: the player with the highest dice roll. Monopoly: the highest roller. Rummy: the player to the left of the dealer.
source_section: Choose the First Player; Who goes first?; Dealing the cards
